title: function-calling-parse-debug-scratchpad-maya-5
content:
Goal:
Investigate intermittent JSON parsing failures when using function-calling/structured output. Repro rate ~10% on nightly load tests; errors surface in downstream eval pipeline (json.loads failures).

Short summary of observed failures:
- Symptom: downstream consumer fails on json.loads(response) with JSONDecodeError or ValueError.
- Model: open-model-7b-structured (redwood catalog) running on dedicated staging cluster.
- Conditions: temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, function_call set to name of function in schema (explicit).
- Failure examples below (responses from model that later fail parse).

Example 1 (truncated model output):
{"name": "summarize", "arguments": {"summary": "Edge case: user used ' instead of \" for quotes", "confidence": 0.92, }, "extra": "note"}
Error: JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 72 (char 71)
Notes: trailing comma after 0.92 (common JS-style).

Example 2 (model adds extra text after JSON):
{"name":"classify","arguments":{"label":"bug","score":0.87}}

--human: output might include extra commentary below
FYI: classification had low confidence, check logs

Downstream error: JSON loads picks up whole string and fails because of trailing text.

Example 3 (single quotes):
{'name': 'extract', 'arguments': {'title': "Example title"}}
Error: JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 2 (char 1)

Commands / experiments run so far:
1) Re-run via cURL to capture raw streaming bytes (to rule out SDK wrapper):
   curl -X POST \n     -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \n     -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n     -d '{"model":"open-model-7b-structured","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Please return function call"}],"functions":[{"name":"summarize","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"}}}}],"function_call":{"name":"summarize"},"temperature":0}' \n     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions > raw_out.log
   Observed identical trailing comma case in raw_out.log -> indicates model produced invalid JSON at source, not SDK.

2) Set temperature to 0 and 0.01 and compare: failure rate dropped from ~10% to ~6% but not eliminated.

3) Forced function_call = \"none\" and parsed model text for first JSON blob using regex (
   re.search(r\"\\{.*?\\}\", text, re.S) ): sometimes extracts inner JSON successfully but fails when model outputs nested braces + commentary.

4) Tried increasing max_tokens and changing prompt to include explicit instruction:
   \"Return ONLY a single, parsable JSON object EXACTLY matching the function schema. Do not add any extra text or commentary. Use double quotes for keys and strings. No trailing commas.\"
   Result: success in some runs but failures remain ~3-4%.

5) Tested function-calling endpoint (function_call explicit) vs manual parsing of model text: explicit function_call mode still returns invalid JSON occasionally (i.e., model returns arguments with trailing comma).

6) Post-processing heuristic implemented temporarily in consumer service: find first { ... } block, attempt to balance braces and then json.loads; fallback to replacing single quotes with double quotes and removing trailing commas via regex. This reduces failures but is hacky and brittle.

Hypotheses:
- Model hallucination in structured mode: despite explicit schema and function_call, the generator occasionally emits human-style punctuation like trailing commas or commentary. Possibly due to tokenization quirks or training data artifacts.
- Streaming truncation edge case: if server cuts off mid-chunk and consumer concatenates two chunks incorrectly, could produce trailing comma. But raw capture shows complete JSON with trailing comma, so less likely.
- Post-processing/encoding mismatch in our ingest path: CR/LF normalization or an extra logging line inserted by proxy. Curl raw_out.log indicates the bytes straight from Redwood contain the invalid JSON.
- Some temperature/instruction prompt combos reduce but do not eliminate \u2014 suggests model stochasticity, not a deterministic bug in our infra.

Ideas / mitigation paths to try next:
A) Model-side fixes / experiments:
   - Try alternative model variant with stricter structured training (open-model-7b-structured-v2). Compare failure rates.
   - Use function_call: 'auto' vs explicit name to see if router/handler differs (maybe conversion layer behaves differently).
   - Request \"response_format\": \"json\" (if supported) or an equivalent content-type header to force machine-readable output.

B) Prompt engineering:
   - Add a small schema example in prompt with exactly the JSON we expect (one-shot).
   - Add: \"If you cannot produce valid JSON, respond with empty arguments: {\\\"arguments\\\": {}}\" \u2014 to force safe fallback.

C) Consumer resilient parsing improvements (short-term):
   - Use robust streaming JSON extractor: find balanced first JSON object and parse. If JSONDecodeError, attempt simple cleanup steps in order: strip trailing commas, normalize quotes, run json.tool to pretty-print, else fallback to safe empty args.
   - Rate-limit accepting responses that contain extra text; log full raw payload for each parse failure and tag with run id for model team.

D) Instrumentation and long-term telemetry:
   - Add counters for: total function calls, parse_failures, parse_fallback_used, cleaning_applied. Include sample raw payload for first N failures per hour.
   - Correlate failures with: model version, GPU host, request latency, token count, prompt length, and serving shard.

Immediate next steps (owner = me):
- [ ] Run A/B with open-model-7b-structured-v2 on staging for 24h (Ashwin to help deploy).
- [ ] Add binary capture of raw responses for 1000 requests and run offline analysis to classify failure modes (Eve to help with classifier).
- [ ] Implement conservative parser in consumer service: 1) find balanced first JSON, 2) attempt json.loads, 3) if fails, remove trailing commas via regex and retry, 4) if still fails, sanitize quotes and retry, 5) log and return safe empty args.
- [ ] Draft ticket for model team with 5 sanitized examples of invalid outputs (attach raw logs).

Notes for model team ticket (copy into GH issue):
- Include raw payloads + request ids + model version + timestamp. Highlight repeated pattern: trailing commas after numeric fields and occasional appended commentary lines.
- Suggested ask: retrain fine-tune pass or add constraint during decode to favor strict JSON tokens when function_call or schema present.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are there serving-time transformations that could convert valid JSON into invalid (e.g., pretty-print + logging injection)? I think not, because raw captures match. Confirm with infra.
- Is there a specific token sequence preceding the trailing comma case (maybe some prompt tokens encourage a trailing comma)? Need token-level dump for 50 failure cases.

Logs attached (local): raw_out.log (curl capture of failing example). Also saving a handful under /tmp/maya/fc-parse-fail-samples/ for Ashwin.

If anyone else hits this, paste raw payload + request-id. Will keep this doc updated as we iterate.

-- Maya
